title: Realtor due-diligence on a DD listing

persona.description: Realtor preparing a marketing package for a downtown Dartmouth property

turns.user_message: Hey, I'm doing due diligence on a listing at 100 Wyse Road in Dartmouth — it's in the DD zone. The current building has ground-floor retail with residential above. Can you confirm that mixed-use setup is actually permitted as-of-right in DD, and are there any restrictions on what types of commercial uses are allowed on the ground floor specifically?

Good to know on the use permissions. Now my buyer is asking about redevelopment potential — if someone wanted to build new or add floors to the existing structure, what's the maximum height allowed in the DD zone and are there any streetwall requirements they'd need to hit? I want to give them a realistic picture of the upside.

One more thing — the current building has a vacant ground-floor commercial unit and the owner was thinking of converting it to residential before selling to boost the income profile. Is that kind of internal conversion from commercial to residential something that would need a full development permit in DD, or does it fall under one of the exemptions? I saw something about internal conversions in DD being potentially exempt but I want to make sure I'm reading that right.
